completion: Dual enrolment Table of contents Taking two study programmes simultaneously Duel enrolment means taking two study programmes simultaneously in order to obtain two separate degree titles. You can take the two study programmes at the same university or study at two different universities in Berlin and Brandenburg. Before taking two study programmes simultaneously, you should think about this carefully — the average workload for a study programme at HTW Berlin is equivalent to a 40-hour work week. Conditions If you apply for two NC (restricted admission) study programmes at the same time and are granted admission to both, you can only choose one study programme. prompt: Tell me about Denied re-registration

prompt: Tell me about Financing your studies
completion: Financing your studies At HTW Berlin, only the following semester fees are charged to those participating in degree programmes. However, it is wise to plan for the financing of living expenses during degree programmes, because students usually need at least 950 euros per month to support themselves financially . Many are financially supported by their parents during their studies, get a part-time job or apply for a BAföG study grant or a scholarship . The precise amount of money required to complete a degree programme depends on several cost factors. The largest proportion is usually accounted for by the accommodation , thus determining the budget available for the remaining expenses. Average monthly expenses Rent including additional costs 400-650 Euro Food 180-250 Euro Clothing variable Learning materials variable Health insurance 130 Euro Telephone, internet, radio and TV license fees 25-60 Euro Leisure, culture, sport variable

completion: Repeating an examination Table of contents Module examinations failed The modules in Bachelor’s and Master’s study programmes are subject to examination. Some modules consist of several units, which are each completed with their own examination. The units are weighted with a percentage and are combined together to form the module grade. A module examination is considered to be failed if you have not received the grade of at least "sufficient" (grade 4.0) or "pass" or the weighted average of the unit grades does not amount to a minimum grade of 4.0. Repeating an examination You can repeat an examination in the second examination period in the same semester or at the latest within the repeatability period. completion: Module registration Table of contents Who is required to enrol in courses? In your first semester , you will automatically be admitted to all compulsory courses, including foreign language courses, according to the sample plan if you are studying full-time. You are responsible for enrolling in supplementary or elective modules. From the second semester onwards , you must enrol in all courses, language courses and supplementary modules yourself. If you are studying part-time , you are responsible for compiling your own study plan. If you are enrolled in a part-time or postgraduate programme at the Division of Continuing Education (ZbwS) , you do not need to enrol on the courses yourself. You will be enrolled automatically. Course enrolment is divided into four phases. Please note that you are not automatically accepted for a place on the course after enrolling. completion: Students with children HTW Berlin supports students with children with organising their studies and is committed to improving the way its study programmes accommodate the daily needs of students with family responsibilities. Table of contents What should I know about maternity protection? The Maternity Protection Act ( Mutterschutzgesetz ) also applies for students. Pregnant women and nursing mothers and their children are protected by law against risks, excessive workloads and detriment to health caused by studying. They are also protected against financial losses and the loss of their study place. Please register your pregnancy as soon as possible with studierendenservice@htw-berlin.de , enclosing a copy of the first page of your maternity passport. with the Safety Engineers of HTW Berlin so that they can initiate a risk assessment. completion: Ask Özgün: FAQ for prospective students FAQ for prospective students Which degree programmes are offered at HTW Berlin? HTW Berlin operates approximately 80 practice-oriented Bachelor’s and Master’s degree programmes . Das Spektrum umfasst Technik, Informatik, Wirtschaft, Gestaltung und Kultur. The range of subject areas offered includes technology, IT, business, design and culture. HTW Berlin also offers a number of degree programmes in English. How are degree programmes organised? How are studies organised in general? Study structure HTW Berlin offers degree programmes leading to a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree. A Bachelor’s degree programme takes 6 or 7 semesters (3 to 3.5 years). Subsequent Master’s programmes take 3 or 4 semesters (1.5 to 2 years). Courses and examinations The degree programme consists of various modules with seminars, tutorials and seminar-style courses (similar to lectures, only smaller).
